diveTitle: What actually happens when you convert to PDF
diveSubtitle: How sheets, formulas and page breaks carry over.
dive1Title: What happens to formulas and calculations
dive1Desc: Formulas convert to their calculated result, not the underlying formula — a cell showing =SUM(A1:A10) becomes a static number in the PDF. This is expected since a PDF is a fixed snapshot; if you need the live formulas, keep the Excel file alongside the PDF.
dive2Title: Multiple sheets — one PDF or several?
dive2Desc: All sheets in your workbook convert into a single PDF, one after another, in the order the tabs appear in Excel. Hidden sheets are skipped by default, matching what you'd see if you printed the workbook directly from Excel.
dive3Desc: A spreadsheet wider than one page gets split across multiple PDF pages, following Excel's own page break logic — the same breaks you'd see using Print Preview in Excel. Setting a print area or adjusting page breaks before converting gives you more control over exactly where pages split.
dive4Desc: Charts convert as visual images exactly as they appear in Excel, and conditional formatting like color scales and data bars carries over since it's rendered visually, not as a live rule. Neither remains interactive or editable in the PDF.
dive5Title: Print area and page setup settings
dive5Desc: If you've set a specific print area, page orientation, or scaling in Excel's Page Layout settings, the conversion respects those — the PDF matches what you'd get from File > Print in Excel, not necessarily the full unformatted sheet.
dive6Title: Merged cells and frozen rows or columns
dive6Desc: Merged cells convert cleanly as a single visual cell spanning the merged area. Frozen rows or columns are a screen-viewing feature only — they don't repeat on every printed page automatically unless you've also set specific print titles in Excel.

seoSection1Title: The Best Way to Convert Excel Spreadsheets to PDF Online
seoSection1Para1: Converting an Excel file to PDF is the most reliable way to make sure it looks the same for everyone. PDFs are universally readable, uneditable, and print perfectly — unlike XLSX files, which depend on the viewer having Excel installed.
seoSection1Para2: The conversion is free, needs no software, and adds no watermark. Formulas become their calculated values, and hidden sheets are skipped by default.
seoSection2Para: One of the trickiest parts of Excel-to-PDF conversion is handling workbooks with multiple sheets and embedded charts. Many basic converters strip charts or only export the active sheet. Our engine processes every tab in your workbook and renders charts, conditional formatting, and pivot tables faithfully into the final PDF.
